Buy an Established Business in India

Buying an established Indian business involves defining the acquisition thesis, finding suitable targets, evaluating the business, arranging funding and agreeing a viable ownership transition. A credible buyer should have clear investment criteria and a decision process.

Start a private enquiry ↗

Start with the reason to acquire

A buyer may seek new customers, manufacturing capacity, intellectual property, geographic access or a business to operate. Define which capability is essential and which can be developed internally. This separates genuine strategic fit from merely attractive financial metrics.

Translate strategy into screening criteria

Set the preferred deal size, ownership stake, minimum earnings or cash-flow requirements, geographic limits and operational capabilities. Decide which risks are unacceptable and who has authority to approve the investment.

Underwrite the standalone business

Review sustainable earnings, working capital, debt, asset condition, customer concentration and management depth. Quantify synergies separately and account for the costs and time required to realise them. A promising target is not automatically a sound transaction.

How Legacy Search can help

We work with acquirers to define their mandate, originate suitable conversations and coordinate the acquisition process with professional advisers. Share an initial acquisition brief rather than confidential financial documentation through the public enquiry form.

Common questions

Can I acquire a majority stake rather than 100%?

Potentially. The appropriate structure depends on the owner’s preferences, governance, financing and applicable law.

Is an acquisition budget the same as enterprise value?

No. Equity purchase price, debt, transaction costs and working-capital requirements must be considered separately.

General information only; not legal, tax or investment advice. Transaction availability, suitability and execution depend on the circumstances.
